key_insight: SAGE-PINN embeds axisymmetric cylindrical geometry, parity-preserving variables, and exact boundary ansätze into a PINN to remove the axis singularity and enforce mass conservation by construction.
engineering_relevance: This enables mesh-free simulation of coupled flow and heat transfer in axisymmetric devices such as stenosed arteries, with no labeled training data and robust performance across varying buoyancy and advection regimes.
method: Use the transformed radial variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforce boundary conditions exactly with analytical boundary-fitted ansätze and train in staged momentum-thermal-joint phases.
Stabilize optimization with residual normalization, Péclet-/Richardson-number continuation, and a physics-scaled drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, the model kept mass conservation at single-precision round-off and achieved up to 1.6% axial-velocity and 9.1% temperature L2 error over the central operating range.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in the extreme regimes of strongly buoyancy-driven slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so continuation and scaling choices may need careful tuning there.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
